key_insight: The paper shows that a fault-tolerant, literature-grounded LLM pipeline can autonomously move from corpus mining to a publication-ready computational physics manuscript while avoiding ungrounded hallucinations.
engineering_relevance: It suggests a practical architecture for high-stakes scientific automation: isolate reasoning in fresh contexts, force numerical confrontation against published references, and use redundancy plus review checkpoints for reliability.
method: Mapped 11,083 condensed-matter arXiv papers to identify a research direction.
Used six phased, fresh-context sessions with only on-disk state shared across sessions.
Calibrated and validated work through reproduction of literature anchors, novel first-principles computations, and adversarial review.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 47 fresh-context sessions, 2,162 literature-consultation events, and a full pipeline producing three substantive physics findings.
watch_item: The approach still depends on successful reproduction of external references, so toolchain gaps or ambiguous literature can become bottlenecks.
paper_title: Grounded autonomous research: a fault-tolerant LLM pipeline from corpus to manuscript in frontier computational physics
